To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the heavy quark suppression factor, R_AA for charm and bottom quark is 0.6 and 0.4, respectively, for 0% - 10% central Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV at RHIC and 5.5 and 2.8 at 0 - 5% central Pb+Pb collisions at 2.76 TeV at LHC.

the drag and diffusion coefficients for charm and bottom quark in QGP have been evaluated and the resulting nuclear suppression factor for single non-photonic electrons resulting from semi-leptonic decay of charm and bottom hadrons has been computed.

the drag and diffusion coefficients for heavy quarks in the QGP are sensitive to their masses, and the nuclear suppression factor of heavy quarks in QGP is sensitive to the masses of the heavy quarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of heavy quarks propagating in quark gluon matter produced in heavy ion collisions at Large Hadtron Collider.
the study of heavy quark transport properties in the QGP and their implications for the heavy quark production in the heavy-ion collisions.
the transport coefficients of heavy quarks and the nuclear suppression factor RAA for heavy quarks in the quark gluon matter produced in heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charm quark suppression at the LHC is consistent with the QGP formation in nuclear collisions at the LHC energies.
the charm and bottom quark RAA at LHC is sensitive to the temperature dependence of the heavy quark diffusion coefficient.

the charm quarks suffer a large suppression in the QGP and this suppression is mainly due to the collisional energy loss, while for the bottom quarks, the collisional energy losses are much smaller and the dominant energy losses arise from radiative energy losses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heavy quark suppression factor, R AA is sensitive to the mass and the LPM suppression of the radiative energy loss.
the LHC data on the non-photons single electron spectra can be well described using the effective drag and diffusions coefficients for charm and bottom quark.
the mass dependence of the RAA is not very strong.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heavy quarks can serve as an excellent probe of QGP properties.
the mass of the heavy quark plays a very important role in the energy loss process.
the LPM effects are significant for the heavy quark energy loss in QGP.
